notes: §1985:XIV.3.2.3 SR1: "Cd-name-1 must reference an input CD when the INPUT phrase is specified." BindDisable calls BindPath, which maps INPUT with or without TERMINAL to a CdRule of formats [Input] and refuses through ResolveCommunicationCd (COBOL6170) a name that is no cd-name and a CD of another format. The witness refuses DISABLE INPUT of an output CD. Probes at --std 85: (b) DISABLE INPUT TERMINAL of an I-O CD refused COBOL6170; DISABLE INPUT of an output CD refused; of a data-name refused; of a containing program's CD from a nested program refused; two cd-names refused COBOL0307; no cd-name refused COBOL0001. (d) DISABLE INPUT CI WITH KEY "PASSWORD" and DISABLE INPUT TERMINAL CI KEY "PW" (WITH omitted) accepted and ran, printing ST=20 and ST=21. (c) the KEY phrase is 85-only: the same program at --std 2002 refused COBOL0902 at KEY; --std 2023 refuses the facility. (a, e, f) not reached: the operand is a cd-name. Every refusal's text cites ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex A rather than the 1985 rule, the cross-cutting citation matter kb/Work PB4950 decides; the outcome is the one the rule requires.

next.reason: 1985: "Cd-name-1 must reference an input CD when the INPUT phrase is specified."; 2023: "No DISABLE statement or communication description entry in 2023; no clause holds the feature". No 2023 clause holds the DISABLE statement or CDs, so the communication module is gone. The wording candidates concern OPEN, SORT, CALL and the like, not DISABLE.
